title: Can an online learner keep write coordinates useful while the resident computation moves?
question: Can a local online learner preserve useful computational identity when the resident coordinate system itself drifts?
hypothesis: If useful identity is a continuation rather than a fixed visible location, an online Sanger-style learner that keeps adapting to streaming resident state should preserve a richer persistent-write/operator-composition family under slow basis drift than the same learner frozen before drift or even a perfect initial modal basis left stale.
assumptions: All adaptive arms receive the same deterministic state streams, dimensionality, fast eigenvalues, drift schedule, write law and evaluation protocol.
The online and frozen Sanger arms start from the same deterministic random basis and are identical through the pre-drift learning period.
The online Sanger update sees only current state samples; it is not given the hidden basis, drift angle or fast matrix.
The stale-oracle arm begins with the exact initial modal basis but is not transported as the modes rotate.
The moving-oracle arm is a positive upper control and is never available to the online learner.

experiments.purpose: Learn resident coordinates online, rotate the hidden modal basis through 1.2 radians, and compare continuous adaptation against an identically pretrained frozen learner, a perfect-but-stale initial basis, and the moving oracle.

attackers.claim_attacked: Initial coordinate learning is enough; continuing adaptation is unnecessary.
A computational identity can be permanently attached to its original coordinate location.
The online learner may appear to improve only because the moving target itself destroys separability for every strategy.

gates.meaning: Continuous online learning must end closer to the current resident coordinate family than its identically pretrained frozen counterpart in at least 7/8 worlds.
Online continuation must preserve a richer written-operator family than freezing the same learner in at least 7/8 worlds.
Online continuation must preserve stronger A→B versus B→A composition separation than the frozen learner in at least 7/8 worlds.
A continually updated imperfect learner must beat an initially perfect modal basis that is left behind as the computation moves.
The continuation advantage must survive the functional composition readout.
The online learner remains bounded by the current-coordinate oracle.
The online composition result remains bounded by the moving oracle.

if_pass: In this constructed slowly drifting recurrent family, continued online Sanger-style coordinate learning preserves the current write/operator organization better than freezing the same learner before drift.

A perfect initial modal basis can become functionally worse than an imperfect basis that continues to adapt, supporting the narrow statement that computational identity behaves like a continuation rather than a fixed coordinate location in this world.
if_fail: The online/local learner does not earn coordinate continuation under the frozen drift gate; the v2 batch-covariance result does not extend to this streaming moving-target setting.
always_limit: The drift is smooth, low-dimensional and slow relative to the learner; the system is still a constructed symmetric linear recurrence.
Periodic Gram-Schmidt stabilization makes this Sanger-style learner online but not strictly synapse-local.
No delayed credit signal is transported yet; this gate tests coordinate identity/continuation, not ThirdWay's full credit-transport claim.

limitations: The hidden mode rotation law is supplied by the synthetic world.
The online learner receives raw state samples but not sparse event-limited observations.
The final operator audit uses the same synthetic write law as v2.
The next gate should add delayed credit or task learning whose eligibility trace must follow the moving coordinates.

provenance.note: Motivates stale-coordinate versus continuing computational identity controls.
Replaces batch/static covariance alignment with streaming learning under coordinate drift.
